data.title: Building a Base Yocto Image for Raspberry Pi Zero 2W
data.description: A step-by-step guide to building and booting a clean base Yocto image for the Raspberry Pi Zero 2W
data.review: A detailed guide covering the entire process of setting up, configuring, and flashing a custom Yocto project image for the Raspberry Pi Zero 2W using the Scarthgap branch.

data.title: Getting Started with the SmartThings API - Environment Setup
data.description: A beginner's guide to setting up your environment for the SmartThings API. This post covers generating tokens and making your first API calls.
data.review: A detailed explanation of the initial setup steps for using the SmartThings API, from issuing a Personal Access Token (PAT) to retrieving a list of registered devices using curl commands.

data.title: Creating a Custom Yocto Layer for Raspberry Pi Zero 2W
data.description: A step-by-step guide to creating and integrating a custom meta-layer to manage your own recipes and configurations in a Yocto build for the Raspberry Pi Zero 2W
data.review: Specific steps for creating and adding your own meta-layer in the Yocto Project to efficiently manage custom images for the Raspberry Pi Zero 2W.

data.title: Defining Custom Image and Distro for Raspberry Pi Zero 2W
data.description: A guide to creating custom image recipes and distribution configurations in your own Yocto layer, eliminating the need for manual local.conf edits
data.review: Learn how to automate manual configurations and efficiently build and manage your own images by adding image recipes and distribution settings to a custom Yocto layer for the Raspberry Pi Zero 2W.

data.title: Enabling GT911 Touchscreen on Raspberry Pi Zero 2W with Yocto
data.description: A step-by-step guide to configuring Yocto recipes and hardware setup for the GT911 touch controller
data.review: A detailed guide on how to enable and configure the GT911 touchscreen via the Yocto Project as part of creating a custom device using a Raspberry Pi Zero 2W and a 7.5-inch E-Ink display.

data.title: Enabling E-Ink Display on Raspberry Pi Zero 2W with Yocto
data.description: A step-by-step guide to enabling the SPI interface and configuring Yocto recipes for E-Paper displays
data.review: Learn how to configure the hardware for the GDEY075T7-T01 E-Ink display on a Raspberry Pi Zero 2W in a Yocto environment, and follow the process of modifying image recipes to install essential Python packages.

data.title: Bash $RANDOM Variable
data.description: Understanding and using the $RANDOM internal variable in Bash, including its open-source implementation
data.review: A detailed explanation of how to use the Bash $RANDOM built-in variable to generate random numbers between 0 and 32767, including how to specify ranges, set seeds, and an analysis of its internal operational principles based on open-source code.

data.title: Building LineageOS 14.1 for Samsung Galaxy Note 8.0 (n5110)
data.description: A guide to configuring a Docker build environment, syncing repositories, and compiling a custom ROM for the n5110
data.review: A step-by-step guide to setting up a LineageOS 14.1 custom ROM build environment, downloading source code, and preparing device-specific code to repurpose an old Samsung Galaxy Note 8.0 (n5110) tablet.

data.title: gcc attribute: constructor & destructor
data.description: Explore the internal process and usage of gcc attributes: constructor (pre-main execution) and destructor (post-main execution).
data.review: Learn how to use GCC constructor and destructor attributes in C to define functions that run automatically before and after main, and how to control their execution order.

data.title: Flashing LineageOS 14.1 for Samsung Galaxy Note 8.0 (n5110)
data.description: A guide to flashing the compiled LineageOS 14.1 ROM and recovery image to the Samsung Galaxy Note 8.0 (n5110).
data.review: A detailed guide on flashing the custom-built LineageOS 14.1 ROM and recovery image to the Samsung Galaxy Note 8.0 (n5110) using the Heimdall tool in a Linux environment, including the device initialization process.

data.title: gcc options: -Wformat
data.description: Explore the -Wformat option in GCC to detect format string errors and security vulnerabilities at compile time.
data.review: Learn how to use the GCC -Wformat option to detect type mismatches and security vulnerabilities when using format strings in functions like printf and scanf during the compilation stage.

data.title: gcc attribute: cleanup
data.description: The cleanup attribute runs a function when a variable goes out of scope. This attribute can only be applied to auto function scope variables.
data.review: Learn how to use the GCC cleanup attribute to define cleanup functions that run automatically when a variable goes out of scope, preventing resource leaks and writing safer code.

data.title: NULL != 0
data.description: Exploring why NULL and 0 are not equivalent in GNU C through pre-processor results and memory analysis.
data.review: An analysis of the differences between NULL and 0 in the GNU C environment, detailing potential risks in variadic functions. It covers size differences in 64-bit environments and precautions for variadic functions.

data.title: gcc attribute: nonnull
data.description: The nonnull attribute specifies that some function parameters should be non-null pointers. This allows the compiler to check at compile-time if a null pointer is passed to these arguments.
data.review: Learn how to detect and prevent NULL pointer arguments at compile-time using the GCC nonnull attribute. This guide covers its usage, limitations, and integration with the -Wnonnull option.

data.title: gcc options: -fsigned-char
data.description: A guide to understanding and using the -fsigned-char and -funsigned-char GCC options to control the signedness of plain char.
data.review: Learn about GCC's -fsigned-char and -funsigned-char options. This post explains how to control the default signedness of plain char, which varies by architecture or compiler settings, and provides recommendations for code portability.

data.title: gcc builtin: alloca
data.description: The alloca() function allocates size bytes of space in the stack frame of the caller. This temporary space is automatically freed when the function that called alloca() returns to its caller.
data.review: Learn in detail about the working principle and usage of the GCC built-in function __builtin_alloca. It explains the pros and cons of allocating memory on the stack instead of the heap, security precautions, and differences from VLA through code.

data.title: gcc builtin: choose_expr
data.description: You can use the built-in function __builtin_choose_expr to evaluate code depending on the value of a constant expression. This built-in function returns exp1 if const_exp, which is an integer constant expression, is nonzero. Otherwise it returns exp2.
data.review: Explore the internal workings and usage of the GCC built-in function __builtin_choose_expr. Learn how to select expressions at compile-time based on conditions with practical examples.

data.title: gcc attribute: format, format_arg
data.description: The format attribute specifies that a function takes printf, scanf, strftime or strfmon style arguments which should be type-checked against a format string.
data.review: Explore in detail how to enable type-checking capabilities like printf and scanf in custom functions using GCC's format and format_arg attributes. We provide a guide to writing safe C code through practical real-world examples and internal workings.

data.title: AI Agents for Beginners - 1. Intro to AI Agents and Agent Use Cases
data.description: A breakdown of AI Agent core components (Environment, Sensors, LLM, Tools, Memory), 7 agent types, when to use agents, and a hands-on Python example with Azure AI Foundry.
data.review: Explains the architecture of AI Agents that enable LLMs to go beyond simple text generation and take real-world actions from the perspective of Environment, Sensors, Actuators, Memory, and Tools. Compares 7 types—Simple Reflex, Model-Based, Goal-Based, Utility-Based, Learning, Hierarchical, and Multi-Agent—using a travel agent example, and introduces the process of implementing your first AI Agent directly with Azure AI Foundry and Python.

data.title: AI Agents for Beginners - 2. Explore Agentic Frameworks
data.description: A comparison of Microsoft Agent Framework and Azure AI Agent Service — modular components, multi-agent collaboration, and when to use each for building production AI agents.
data.review: Compare how AI Agent Frameworks differ from traditional AI, as well as the differences between Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) and Azure AI Agent Service. Learn how to prototype quickly using Modular Components, multi-agent collaboration, and Real-Time Learning, alongside ideal use cases for each platform and Python code examples.

data.title: AI Agents for Beginners - 3. Agentic Design Patterns
data.description: A guide to Agentic Design Principles (Space, Time, Core) and three practical patterns — Clear Instructions, Structured Output, and Single Responsibility — for building effective AI agents.
data.review: An introduction to Agentic Design Principles (Space, Time, Core) to follow when designing AI Agents, along with three implementation patterns (Clear Instructions, Structured Output, Single Responsibility) and Travel Agent sample code.

data.title: AI Agents for Beginners - 4. Tool Use Design Pattern
data.description: How AI agents use tools via function calling — building blocks, tool schemas, approval modes, and practical examples with Microsoft Agent Framework and Azure AI Agent Service.
data.review: A deep dive into the Tool Use Design Pattern for AI Agents. Covers how Function/Tool Calling works, building blocks (Schema, Execution, State), using the @tool decorator, maintaining human oversight with approval_mode, and configuring Knowledge/Action Tools in Azure AI Agent Service with Python examples.

data.title: AI Agents for Beginners - 5. Agentic RAG
data.description: Agentic RAG — how LLMs autonomously decide when and how to retrieve information, iterate with a maker-checker loop, self-correct, and deliver high-quality grounded responses.
data.review: Summarizes the core concepts of Agentic RAG. Explores differences from traditional RAG, iterative Maker-Checker loops, tool integration and memory, self-correction mechanisms, practical use cases, and governance alongside Python code examples.

data.title: AI Agents for Beginners - 6. Building Trustworthy AI Agents
data.description: How to build safe and trustworthy AI agents — system message framework, threat mitigation, and human-in-the-loop patterns for secure, reliable agentic systems.
data.review: Covers how to build trustworthy AI agents. Explores designing safe prompts with the Meta System Message Framework, mitigating five key threats including Prompt Injection and Knowledge Base Poisoning, and maintaining user oversight with Human-in-the-Loop patterns, complete with Python code examples.

data.title: AI Agents for Beginners - 7. Planning Design Pattern
data.description: How to build planning agents that decompose complex goals into structured subtasks, route work to specialized agents, and iteratively re-plan based on real-world feedback.
data.review: Covers the Planning Design Pattern: decomposing complex goals into subtasks, generating plans with Pydantic structured outputs, routing work to specialized agents via multi-agent orchestration, and iteratively re-planning based on user feedback, complete with Python code examples.

data.title: AI Agents for Beginners - 8. Multi-Agent Design Pattern
data.description: Multi-agent design patterns — when to use them, building blocks of agent communication and coordination, Group Chat / Hand-off / Collaborative Filtering patterns, and a WorkflowBuilder pipeline walkthrough.
data.review: Covers multi-agent design patterns: advantages over single agents (Specialization, Scalability, Fault Tolerance), implementation building blocks like agent communication, coordination, and visibility, three core patterns (Group Chat, Hand-off, Collaborative Filtering), and how to build sequential pipelines using WorkflowBuilder with Python code examples.

data.title: AI Agents for Beginners - 9. Metacognition in AI Agents
data.description: Metacognition in AI agents — self-reflection, corrective RAG, pre-emptive context loading, goal bootstrapping, intent-aware search, code generation, and SQL as RAG.
data.review: Covers metacognition in AI agents. Summarizes the principles of self-reflection, error correction, and strategy adjustment, compares Corrective RAG and Pre-emptive Context Load, and details goal-based plan bootstrapping, intent-aware search, code generation agents, and SQL as RAG techniques alongside Python code examples.

data.title: AI Agents for Beginners - 10. AI Agents in Production: Observability & Evaluation
data.description: How to move AI agents from prototype to production — observability with traces and spans, key metrics, OpenTelemetry instrumentation, offline/online evaluation, cost management, and a real expense claim demo.
data.review: Covers core patterns for deploying AI agents to production, including trace- and span-based observability, key metrics such as latency, cost, errors, and feedback, OpenTelemetry instrumentation, offline and online evaluation loops, cost management strategies, and a hands-on expense claim receipt processing example with Python code.

data.title: AI Agents for Beginners - 11. Using Agentic Protocols (MCP, A2A and NLWeb)
data.description: MCP, A2A, and NLWeb — three agentic protocols for standardized tool access, agent-to-agent collaboration, and natural language interfaces on the web.
data.review: Covers three agentic protocols: MCP enables AI Agents to access external tools and data in a standardized manner, A2A allows agents across diverse frameworks to collaborate, and NLWeb adds natural language interfaces to websites so AI Agents can explore and leverage content. Accompanied by Python code examples.

data.title: AI Agents for Beginners - 12. Context Engineering
data.description: How Context Engineering differs from Prompt Engineering, the five types of context in AI Agents, practical management strategies, and how to recognize and fix Context Poisoning, Distraction, Confusion, and Clash failures.
data.review: Context Engineering for AI Agents - Prompt Engineering vs Context Engineering, Types of Context, Strategies, Common Context Failures(Poisoning, Distraction, Confusion, Clash), Chat Summarization with Agent Scratchpad.

data.title: AI Agents for Beginners - 13. Memory for AI Agents
data.description: Memory types for AI Agents (Working, Short-term, Long-term, Persona, Episodic, Entity, Structured RAG), implementation with Mem0, Cognee, and Azure AI Search, and the self-improving agent pattern with code examples.
data.review: Memory for AI Agents — Understanding Working/Short-term/Long-term/Persona/Episodic/Entity Memory types, Mem0/Cognee Knowledge Graph/Azure AI Search implementation, self-improving agent patterns, and Microsoft Agent Framework code examples.

data.title: AI Agents for Beginners - 14. Microsoft Agent Framework
data.description: Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) core concepts — Agents, Threads, Middleware, Memory, Observability — and advanced workflow patterns including Sequential, Concurrent, Handoff orchestration, Middleware injection, and Human-in-the-Loop with code examples.
data.review: Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) — Agent creation, execution, threads, middleware, memory, observability, workflows (Executor/Edge/Event), Sequential, Concurrent, and Handoff orchestration patterns, with Human-in-the-Loop implementation code examples.

data.title: AI Agents for Beginners - 15. Computer Use Agent (CUA)
data.description: Build a Computer Use Agent (CUA) with Browser-Use and Playwright via CDP integration. Covers vision-based navigation, structured Pydantic extraction, Agent vs Actor pattern selection, and a real-world Airbnb price comparison workflow.
data.review: Build a Computer Use Agent (CUA) with Browser-Use + Playwright CDP integration — GPT-4 Vision-based web navigation, structured Pydantic output extraction, Agent vs. Actor pattern selection, and a real-world Airbnb price comparison workflow code example.
